title: Hmong Wordnet
name: HmongWN
tagline: White Hmong and Green Mong, linked to the Interlingual Index

main.description: Main lexical database: White Hmong, Green Mong and English.

provenance.description: Per-row source attribution: which source each entry came from.

about.intro:
A wordnet for White Hmong (Hmoob Dawb, mww) and Green Mong (Hmoob Ntsuab, hnj), built from a Hmong semantic ontology and five further sources, and linked to the Collaborative Interlingual Index so that an English, Chinese or Thai word and a Hmong word can be looked up through the same concept. 2,094 of 3,095 White Hmong senses are linked, over 1,592 concepts.

Green Mong is barely present. 96 lemmas and 15 concepts is a token presence rather than a lexicon, and almost all of it is classifiers and kinship terms. The Green Mong vocabulary is the largest single gap in this resource.

The lexicon includes the numeral classifier inventory, 235 forms. Classifiers are not referential, so they carry the part of speech x and are attached to the concept classifier by exemplifies rather than by hypernymy; the nouns each one may quantify are given as classifies relations, with classified by in the other direction. Each classifier is labelled in the five-way scheme of Bond and Paik (2000), in White's own subclasses, and in Bisang's, which follows T'sou (1976), so that any of the three analyses can be recovered.

Every link records the evidence it rests on: 1,710 senses rest on a hand-made concept-set identifier, two independent glosses intersecting, or several languages' wordnets agreeing, and 384 on a single monosemous gloss, which is weaker and is labelled as such. A further 1,001 senses are here unlinked, with their glosses and their semantic category, and 134 of those are staged as annotation sheets in the repository. No fluent speaker has yet checked any of the links.
about.citation: If you use this resource, please cite the hmong-ontology repository and White (2021) for the ontology and the classifier, kinship and underspecified-noun data, and Bisang (1993) for the measure words and class nouns.
about.languageData: The lexical data comes from the hmong-ontology repository (Nathan M. White, Language and Culture Research Centre, James Cook University), released under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. The classifier inventory, the kinship paradigm and the classifier-specified compounds are from White (2021), chapter 7 and Tables 29 and 39–41, which is the base analysis; Bisang (1993), Appendices I and II, supplies the measure words White excludes and the class nouns, with a few further forms from the repository's own stopword list and from studyhmong.com. Vocabulary and Concepticon concept-set identifiers come from the World Loanword Database's White Hmong list (Ratliff), CC BY 4.0. Sense-anchored translations and the translations of the same senses into 25 other languages come from Wiktionary through DBnary, CC BY-SA. Kinship concepts English does not lexicalise are identified by KinDiv, CC BY-SA 3.0.
